card: This PR replaces the BCC and eBPF tracing toolchain in USDT functional tests with GDB. Testing USDT probes previously required BCC, host kernel headers, and root privileges to load BPF programs, which prevented unprivileged local execution and required a privileged Docker container in ASan CI. Tracing through GDB verifies probe metadata, triggers, and argument values without elevated permissions while removing roughly 660 lines of embedded BPF and CI code. The trade-off is that external eBPF loading paths are not exercised and LeakSanitizer must be disabled on the traced children due to ptrace limitations.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided; the implementation matches the previous description.
evidence: PR description: 'All five tests can run with GDB and binutils, without BCC or matching kernel headers. The ASan CI job no longer needs a privileged container and uses SYS_PTRACE instead. This also removes the embedded BPF programs from the tests, reducing their size and maintenance burden. Overall, the change removes roughly 660 lines of test and CI code.'
problem: USDT functional tests require BCC, matching kernel headers, and root/BPF permissions. This makes tracepoint tests difficult to run locally and requires a privileged container in the ASan CI task.

risk.why: Only touches functional tests, CI configurations, and tracing documentation; a bug could cause CI or test runner failures without risking node runtime or consensus.

scope_notes: Touches only functional test infrastructure, documentation, and CI configuration; no production node code is modified.
summary: Replaces the BCC and eBPF tracing framework in USDT functional tests with GDB. Tested nodes run as debugger children that enable tracepoints and inspect probe arguments when hit. This removes dependencies on the BCC toolchain, matching host kernel headers, and elevated BPF privileges, allowing CI containers to drop privileged mode.
